entities.name: Enterovirus meningitis
observations: Acute febrile meningitis with headache, photophobia, neck discomfort, and fine erythematous rash is characteristic of enteroviral infection.
CSF commonly shows lymphocytic pleocytosis, modest protein elevation, and preserved glucose; the case has 72 leukocytes/mm3, 75% lymphocytes, protein 50 mg/dL, and glucose 70 mg/dL.

entities.name: Tuberculous meningitis
observations: Less likely because the presentation is acute and CSF glucose is preserved rather than low; tuberculosis typically has a more subacute course and higher protein.
Differential comparison from the clinical search found no supportive features in this case.

entities.name: Cryptococcal meningitis
observations: Less likely because cryptococcal or other fungal meningitis is usually subacute or chronic and often has higher protein and reduced CSF glucose.
No immunocompromising history or compatible exposure is provided.
